newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour holds on to Euro-parliament seat.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour holds on to Euro-parliament seat.

text.p: Britain's opposition Labour Party easily won a by-election for the European Parliament seat of Merseyside West, although turnout was the lowest for a British election in over 50 years, official results showed on Friday.
Only 11.4 percent of the constituency's 515,549 voters cast their ballots on Thursday, reflecting traditional apathy towards what is widely regarded an irrelevant body.

As expected, Labour's Richard Corbett won the northwest England seat, gaining 31,484 votes. Conservative Jeremy Myers followed with 12,780 while Liberal Democrat Kiron John Cuchulain Reid trailed in third place with 8,829.
"I am delighted to have been elected and look forward to serving this constituency. Europe matters, and nowhere more so than in this constituency," Corbett said.
The by-election followed the death of Labour Member of the European Parliament Ken Stewart in September.

Labour is part of the Socialist group, which with 215 seats is the largest faction in Europe's 626-seat parliament, ahead of the Christian Democrats with 182 seats. The parliament's seat is in the French city of Strasbourg.
Labour also held onto the Barnsley East seat on Thursday in a national parliamentary by-election, wiping out Prime Minister John Major's majority in the House of Commons lower chamber of parliament.
